Research decision D2 proposed a leaf-resolving containment predicate (realpath -m --relative-to=PROJECT_ROOT on the pathspec itself). Verified empirically in a scratch repo during planning: an in-repo leaf symlink whose target lies outside the repo is a LEGAL git add argument (rc=0, staged as a symlink), so D2's form would have dropped it -- a false-positive regression against current behavior. Corrected in the plan to resolve the pathspec's PARENT directory only, verified against 13 pathspec shapes to agree with git add's own accept/reject verdict on every one.

Research decision D7 claimed drop-and-warn beats the status quo on BOTH axes without needing a new exit code, relying on D5's caller-side exit-code branch to surface the violation. Traced during planning: in the exact observed-damage shape (26 valid + 4 out-of-repo paths), the post-fix outcome is exit 0 with a successful commit, so the caller branch never fires and the violation reaches no durable channel -- D7's surface-the-violation axis is traded away for precisely the motivating case. Plan adds a narrow, additive exit code 6 (commit created AND at least one out-of-repository drop) to close it, and reserves exit 7 for task 336's Containment follow-up instead of D5's exit 6.

Research D5 directed the caller-side fix to force a non-terminal status via orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's existing clamp_mode/monotonic-max machinery. That mechanism cannot serve this purpose: clamp_mode is consumed by WORK (f)'s status write at ~line 1137-1264, roughly 560 lines BEFORE the commit at ~1824, and monotonic-max prevents a demotion by construction. Plan delivers the visible-and-attributable half in full (named ERROR, durable issues.jsonl entry, emitted note field) and files the status-demotion half as follow-up (c), which requires reordering WORK (f)/(i) or a sanctioned write out of terminal completed.

A five-minute scratch-repo probe (git init, a leaf symlink out, a symlinked dir, an absolute cross-tree path) settled three design questions the research report had left to analytic reasoning: it reproduced the whole-list git add abort directly, proved the leaf-symlink false-positive in the proposed predicate, and confirmed the through-symlink case is independently fatal to git and should be dropped. Cheap empirical verification beat a second research round.

Research's caller enumeration named two live script callers of git-commit-scoped.sh. A sweep of every non-test .sh found a third: scripts/lib/redeploy-checkpoint-lib.sh, sourced by orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, committing state.json plus TODO.md under the same || echo non-blocking idiom. Like orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh it passes fixed literals only and is unexposed to this defect, so the ruling is unchanged -- but it needs a reasoned allowlist entry in the plan's Phase 5 lint, which a two-caller enumeration would have missed and left the lint failing its own first run.

V8's pre-commit intent snapshot in git-commit-scoped.sh uses 'git hash-object' on each enumerated path, which FOLLOWS a symlink and hashes the pointed-to file's content; the blob git actually commits for a symlink is the raw target-path string instead. The two never match, so V8 unconditionally reports a false 'present with different content' mismatch (exit 5) for EVERY symlink this script commits, regardless of whether the target is in-repo or out-of-repo. Verified by direct reproduction against an in-repo symlink target. Orthogonal to the out-of-repository containment fix this task delivers; not fixed here -- V9 does not touch V8's snapshot mechanism. Recorded as a follow-up candidate for whoever next touches V8.
